text: Grapes, raisins and currants can cause sudden kidney failure in dogs and cats. No safe amount is known. Do not feed. Call a vet or poison hotline immediately if eaten.
Chocolate contains theobromine, which is toxic to dogs and cats. Dark chocolate and baking chocolate are the most dangerous. Do not feed. Contact a vet if eaten.
Onions, garlic, chives and leeks damage red blood cells in dogs and cats, especially cats. Do not feed, including in cooked leftovers.

Xylitol, a sweetener found in sugar-free gum and some peanut butters, causes dangerous drops in blood sugar and liver failure in dogs. Check peanut butter labels before using it for treats or pill pockets.
All parts of true lilies are highly toxic to cats and can cause kidney failure. Keep lilies away from cats entirely.
